segmenti.tekst: إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

segmenti.tekst: أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp, to warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

So, brothers, respected congregation, one of the hardest things for a person is to hear that other people do not love him, to hear that other people cannot stand him. But believe me, there is something that is more dangerous and worse than that.

Worse than that is when people flee from a certain person, so that when they see him approaching a gathering, they disperse. When he arrives unexpectedly, they fall silent, fall silent. When they meet him and cannot avoid him, they give him a sour smile.
Not because, dear brothers, he is poor, not because he is uneducated, but out of fear of his harm, his evil.

There are many such examples today, dear brothers, in our town, our city, our country, where people are afraid of certain people, fearing their harm. Fearing their harm. And you will see, if we have some situation in the city, in society, few are those who dare to say anything. One says: “By Allah, I work in a school, I don't dare say anything.”

Another says: “I have a shop, excuse me, I don't dare say anything.” And so on, and so forth. Dear brothers, an example for us is this landfill that we have in Avlije. You will rarely see anyone speak up about it. And that is precisely out of fear, out of that fear: “I'll lose my job, they'll close my shop, I don't dare do this, I don't dare do that.” And then people flee from those people who can cause harm.

What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say about such people? The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: “Inna sharra an-nasi 'indallahi manzilatan yawm al-qiyamati man tarakahu an-nasu ittiqa'a sharrihi.” He says: the worst people, the most hated people on the Day of Judgment, the most hated with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, are those people, are those whom people avoided out of fear of their harm, their
evil. Out of fear of their harm, their evil. So when he comes, someone says: “Just so I don't get into it with him,” and then a person doesn't comment, doesn't talk.

Out of fear, out of fear… There are many such examples, many such examples today, dear brothers. We have simply fallen into some [unclear] and we cannot get out of it. We cannot get out of it. In another narration it says: “The worst with Allah on the Day of Judgment,” he said, “are those people whom people avoided out of fear of their vulgarity.”
Their vulgarity. And you will see a person so vulgar that when he comes to some place, people disperse. He doesn't care at all, it doesn't interest him.
Will he swear at you? Will he say an ugly word to you? Will he slander you? You cannot stand with him and exchange two words without him insulting you.

A person should pay attention to these things. Wallahi, a person should pay attention to these things. So that he does not end up in the same line with Pharaoh, with Abu Jahl, with the worst people on the Day of Judgment. So that he is not the most hated.

And when you are the most hated, then a person knows roughly what follows after, after… that. A person must by no means allow that. It is said: once a funeral procession passed by the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and his companions, and the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said:

“Mustarihun wa mustarahun minhu.” He said: one who has found rest, and one from whom others have found rest. The companions said: “What does that mean, O Prophet? What does that mean?” The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: the one who has found rest – he has found rest from this world – the believer, a good man, from the hardships of this world and everything that is in this world, from trials, he has found rest; when he passes away, he finds rest.
When a person passes away, he finds rest in the grave. The one from whom others have found rest – others have found rest from his [unclear], his harassment, his ugly words, and so on, and so forth.

They have found rest from him, he said, the people, and the animals, and the trees, and the land. Everyone has found rest from him. That is why the believer must not allow himself this. A father must not allow himself to be such that, when he is not at home, his household rejoices that he is not at home.

A member of the congregation must not allow that, when he is not at the mosque, the congregation rejoices that he is not at the mosque. That they say: “Thank Allah he isn't here, he didn't come here to… thank Allah, he's not here, there's no one to insult us, no one to harass us.” When such a person doesn't come for coffee with other people, where they usually gather, they say: “Thank Allah, he's not here.” Yes, a believer, a sensible human being, must not allow himself this, allow himself this. And the Day of Judgment is surely near. Perhaps we think

it is not near, but it is near. “Iqtarabat as-sa'ah,” says Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in the Qur'an. He says: the Hour of reckoning, He says, has drawn near, it is very near. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was a sign of it fourteen hundred years ago. That is why every person should be careful about his behavior, about his iman (faith), about his family, about his community, about what he has taken on, how he will lead, in what way he will lead, and not have people afraid of him and his evil. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among the true believers. I ask Him, the Exalted, to make us among those who respect, cherish and love

others. I ask Him, the Exalted, to make us among those who are obedient to their parents, I ask Him, the Exalted, to make us among those who are good husbands, good fathers. I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive us the sins of our parents, I ask Him, the Exalted, to help our brothers everywhere, especially our brothers in Gaza. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to help them, to ease their hardships, to free them from these sufferings. I ask Him, the Exalted, to unite us in Jannah (Paradise) as He has united us today in this, in this place.

آمِينَ يَا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لِي وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْعَظِيمِ وَنَفَعَنِي وَإِيَّاكُمْ بِمَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: Amen, O Lord of the worlds. May Allah bless me and you through the Mighty Qur’an and benefit me and you with the verses and the wise reminder it contains. I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
